observation.visible_scene: A single translucent, pale pinkish-white dome-shaped object (rounded, glossy top with two bright specular highlights) rests centered on a flat red circular surface bordered by a cream/white rim. The background is a uniform, featureless light gray. The composition stays the same throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The scene is essentially near-static: the dome keeps the same position relative to the red disc and rim across all frames, with no translation, rotation, or large deformation.

Only very subtle changes in the dome's silhouette and in the thin red liquid ring at its base are discernible over time (slight apparent settling/flattening of the top edge and a marginal widening of the red pool around the base), consistent with a very slow ongoing surface change rather than a discrete event.

Small pixel-level shifts of the whole object-and-rim within the frame (e.g., the left cream rim and the dome's horizontal position move a few pixels between adjacent frames) indicate minor camera jitter/handheld framing drift, not object motion; the gray background itself shows no parallax or change.
Specular highlight positions on the dome wobble slightly frame-to-frame, matching the camera jitter rather than a separate moving light or object.
outside_clip_unknowns: The material identity of the dome and the red liquid (not confirmable from the frames).
Whether the faint shape change is melting, sublimation, or simply lighting/blur, and whether it began before or continues after this segment.
Any cause or trigger for the slow change, and the final state of the object.
uncertain_details: Whether the tiny apparent growth of the red pool at the base is real or an artifact of focus/blur and framing jitter.
Whether the small frame-to-frame position shifts are purely camera motion or include a slight object settle; background evidence is too uniform to disambiguate.
